summary: Up 0.1 on w14 (8.4), which puts PY at the 8.5 target with no high-severity issues. Both w14 medium issues are fixed by the post-rating swatch changes. (1) The trim-A ear chips are now pointed and notched, with a wide size spread and visible fine flecks. They no longer read as polka dots. The p4 ear crop gives cover 16.4 % (py_37305 16.9 %), ground #4a4d5b S 0.18 (photo #4e505f S 0.17), p90/p50 1.55 (1.60), hp 0.219 (0.242), and 102 of 148 blobs are under 8 px (photo 199 of 254). (2) The back weave contrast has come back down to the photo. In p8 the back gives p90/p50 1.34 (py_37301 1.28; w14 1.39), hp 0.191 (0.187; w14 0.219) and S 0.24 (0.22; w14 0.26). The ear-ground colour (a w14 low) is also fixed. Remaining differences: (a) Close up (p5, the p8 cushion, the q13b foreground) the trim-A cloth is still soft square blocks. py_37301 shows fine ribbed dashes, and the p8 cushion hp is 0.129 vs 0.182 there. (b) The pocket geometry and parts are unchanged: about 0.11 m of plain shell under the recess, a light-grey tray rim, a plain holder plate and a blank leaflet. (c) The navy flap is still dead flat (std 1.3 vs 4.6). (d) The placards are blank. (e) At cabin distance (q13) the ears read a little busier and brighter-speckled than in py_37302, where the petals barely register. The colour of the back weave blocks is right, but they are about 1.5-2x coarser than py_37301 at matched framing.
lighting_note: Not scored. After 2913db8 the PY block in q13 still reads cobalt. The flap in q13 is #35416c against #283769 in py_37302, and the backs are S 0.30 against 0.34 at a similar luminance, so the gap is now mostly hue, not saturation. Studio p8 is close to the photo (S 0.24 vs 0.22), so most of the remaining blue cast is the cabin light or tone curve, not material. q14 still has the bright rhombus-shaped sun or specular patch on the far window seat back (around x 500, y 330), so the window sun LUT needs checking. The q13b foreground seat top is very dark between blocks (low-pocket AO may be leaking onto the fabric).
